newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA CALL MONEY ENDS STEADY, GILTS STEADY TO FIRM.
newsitem.headline: INDIA CALL MONEY ENDS STEADY, GILTS STEADY TO FIRM.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 4.5-5.0 percent, unchanged from opening quotes, while securities were steady to up in moderate trade, dealers said.
They said market attention was mainly focussed on an auction of eight-year central government bonds for 30 billion rupees to be held by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) later on Monday.

"Call money is pretty stable at the moment," said a private sector bank dealer. "Demand and supply of funds is evenly matched. But it is not immediately clear whether call money will firm up tomorrow after the auction."
Successful bidders at the bond auction make payment Tuesday.
"But even though there is an outflow towards the bonds tomorrow, what will determine call money is the bids accepted at today's repo auction," the dealer said.
The RBI holds a repo auction later today and reverses last Friday's repo tomorrow.
"The net flows -- difference between today's bids and tommorow's repurchase -- will determine call tomorrow," the dealer said.
Dealers said prices of government securities were steady to firm in moderate trade.
The 12.59 percent 2004 bond was the most actively traded stock, they said.
The bond traded between 106.32 and 106.65 rupees against its last close of 106.25, dealers said.

"There has been active trade in the 12.59 percent 2004 bond, particularly from some primary dealers," said a public sector bank dealer. "It seems some market players are taking positions in this bond ahead of the auction."
"If the yield on today's bond is lower than expected, there will be a rally tomorrow and these guys will make a killing," he said.

Among other stocks, the 11.83 percent 2003 traded between 103.20 and 103.28 against 103.10, the 13.82 percent 2002 traded at 110.58 against 110.52 and the 10.85 percent 2001 rose to 100.70 from 100.60.
